label: early input-phase steps right after an m or x (weaker after d/1/o)
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t<=5) & (isin(prev_tok, [tok("m"), tok("x"), tok("d"), tok("1"), tok("o")]) | isin(prev2_tok, [tok("m"), tok("x")]))
explanation: Fires almost only in the original-input phase (95% of mass; about 5% at the <DEL> step, nearly none during copying). It never fires at t=0, and its rate falls steadily from t=1 (27%) to about zero by t>=7. The main driver is the previous input token: after m (42% rate, 7x lift) or x (38%, 6x) it fires in about 88% of steps with t<=5, and these steps make up the top-activation quartile (e.g. m m z gives 1.0 at z). It fires more weakly after d, 1 and o, and leaves a smaller trailing activation two steps after an m/x. The predicate (input phase, t<=5, previous token in {m,x,d,1,o} or token two back in {m,x}) gets dev P=0.59, R=0.73, F1=0.66, mass recall 0.86. Magnitude is largest right after m/x early in the sequence and drops with position. The missed activations are mostly small (<0.2 of max) firing at early positions after other tokens. Many false positives are later-position or d/1/o-context steps where it stays silent. It does not respond to the current input token identity (flat in_tok lift) or to the output token.
